subtype: Approach: copying a friend's path without fit [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Pradeep, and yes, I'll tell you about the fifteen thousand rupees I burned. My roommate Ira got into a big service company right after a coaching course on aptitude tests, and I thought, that's the path. So I signed up, same course, same fee, and sat through six weeks of number puzzles. I'm a design student. I make posters and app screens, and in that classroom I felt like a fish on a bicycle. When I started applying, the roles I liked wanted a portfolio, not puzzle scores. Ira's road and mine were different roads. The course wasn't bad. It just wasn't mine, and I only worked that out after paying for it. Now I'm building a portfolio of three projects instead.

qa.q: How long was the coaching course that Pradeep took?
qa.a: The course was six weeks of number puzzles.

qa.q: How did Pradeep feel during the course?
qa.a: Pradeep felt out of place, like a fish on a bicycle, since the puzzles did not suit a design student.

qa.q: What could Pradeep have done instead of copying Ira's course?
qa.a: Pradeep could have started from a personal strength, design, and built a portfolio while looking at design role listings.

qa.q: How might Ira see Pradeep's experience?
qa.a: Ira may feel surprised or a little sorry that a path that worked for Ira did not fit Pradeep, since the two of them have different strengths. 🙂

grounding: Because a roommate got into a service company through a coaching course, a student pays for the same course although the student's strength is design and the roles differ.

subtype: Approach: copying a friend's path without fit [Pitfall]
passage: I'm Jahnavi. Last year I got my job at a big IT services company after a three-month coaching course in aptitude and basic coding. My roommate Sabina watched the whole thing. This year, she signed up for the same course, paid the fee from her savings, and started the same timetable. The strange part: Sabina's the best designer in our batch. Her sketchbook is full of app screens; she redesigned the college fest website on her own. But every evening she sat with aptitude worksheets and sighed. When I asked why she was doing it, she said, "It worked for you." In week five she skipped a class to finish a poster for a friend's small startup, and looked happier than I'd seen her all month. I don't know what she really wants. But I'm not sure my road was ever hers.

qa.q: What did Sabina redesign on her own?
How does Sabina seem to feel about the aptitude worksheets?
qa.a: Sabina seems bored and unhappy with them, sighing every evening, and far happier when she is designing.

qa.q: What else could Sabina do instead of copying the course?
qa.a: Sabina could look at design roles, build a portfolio from the sketchbook and fest work, and ask a placement advisor which path fits design.

qa.q: How does Jahnavi see Sabina following the same path?
qa.a: Jahnavi is uneasy about it, doubting that a route that suited Jahnavi fits Sabina's real strength in design.

grounding: Shows a student paying for the same coaching course that got a roommate a services job, although the student's strength is design and the roles differ.

subtype: Approach: copying a friend's path without fit [Pitfall]
passage:
June. Usha came home with an offer letter from a large services company and a certificate from the coaching course she'd done. Vasudha, her roommate, looked at the certificate for a long time. That night she enrolled in the same course and paid the fee.
August. Vasudha sat through her fourth mock coding test and scored low again. Her notebook margins were full of tiny drawings of app screens. Usha noticed. "You're redesigning the test page instead of solving the test," she joked. Vasudha didn't laugh.
October. A design studio visited campus looking for interface design interns. The brief asked for a portfolio. Vasudha had sketches but nothing finished, because every evening since June had gone into aptitude drills. She submitted three rough screens. On the walk back she said quietly, "I spent four months on your road, Usha. Mine was right here in the margins."

qa.a: A design studio looking for interface design interns.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling on the walk back?
qa.a: Vasudha felt regretful and a little sad, realising four months went into a path that didn't fit.

qa.q: What would you change first if you were Vasudha in June?
qa.a: Ask what the roles actually need and what you are good at, then put the evenings into a design portfolio instead of copying the course.

qa.q: How might Usha feel hearing your road?
qa.a: Usha may feel awkward or sad, never having meant for Vasudha to copy her, and might wish they had talked about it in June.

grounding: Illustrates a student copying a roommate's coaching-course route into a services job despite a strength in design, and missing a design chance.
